en.title: Mind Control: Neuralink Participant Plays GTA VI With His Thoughts
en.summary: A groundbreaking demonstration shows a Neuralink participant navigating the world of Grand Theft Auto VI using only his mind. This advancement offers a glimpse into a future where brain-computer interfaces could revolutionize gaming accessibility.
en.body:
The sprawling, meticulously crafted world of **Grand Theft Auto VI** is now accessible in a way previously confined to science fiction, thanks to **Neuralink**. A participant in the company's clinical trial has shared a remarkable video showcasing their ability to play the latest Rockstar Games title using only their thoughts.

This two-minute highlight reel, shared by Neuralink, demonstrates the participant navigating the vibrant landscapes of Leonida, engaging in boat chases, aerial maneuvers, and intense shootouts. The technology translates neural signals into game inputs, allowing for fluid control that the participant describes as transformative. Previously, he relied on a mouth stick and an iPad, a method that was physically taxing and limiting. "Before the old chip and surgery, I was using a mouth stick and an iPad," he explained. "I was essentially like a bird, just pecking at an iPad. There was a few games I could play, but obviously, it made your jaw sore and everything sore. So then, I get a chip, and it's like, 'What does this let me do?' Immediately, controlling a computer is like, 'boom.' Portal to the world. You just immediately get your portal to the world back."

## A New Era for Accessibility

This demonstration is particularly poignant given the immense detail **Rockstar Games** poured into **GTA VI**. The game's unprecedented level of realism and freedom has captivated millions, but for individuals with severe mobility challenges, such experiences have often been out of reach. The **Neuralink** implant offers a tangible solution, restoring a sense of agency and interaction with digital worlds. The participant's ability to steer a speedboat and pilot a plane with such apparent ease underscores the potential of brain-computer interfaces to break down barriers in entertainment and beyond. While the video doesn't confirm the specific console used, it highlights the successful integration of **Neuralink** technology with a major, contemporary gaming title.

## Community and Future Implications

The gaming community has long advocated for greater accessibility, and this development has sparked considerable excitement and discussion. While the **Neuralink** technology is still in its early stages, part of an "extremely limited clinical trial," as the company reiterated, its potential impact is undeniable. This demonstration moves beyond simpler control schemes and shows a sophisticated level of interaction with a complex 3D environment. The implications extend far beyond gaming, offering hope for enhanced communication and control for individuals with paralysis or other severe motor impairments.

## What's Next

**Neuralink** has stated that its devices are investigational and not yet approved by regulatory bodies. Further details on the expansion of the clinical trial and the broader availability of this technology have not yet been announced. However, this successful demonstration in **Grand Theft Auto VI** marks a significant milestone in the journey toward more inclusive and advanced human-computer interaction.

content_raw: A Neuralink participant has shared a video showcasing how the technology has allowed him to drive boats, fly planes, and get in shootouts in GTA 6 with his mind. Neuralink shared a video of one of its few participants playing Rockstar Games' latest on social media yesterday. The two-minute highlight reel showed how the individual can use the brain implant tech to take Jason through Leonida with ease, saying that previous methods would often leave him sore. "I was essentially like a bird, just pecking at an iPad. There was a few games I could play, but obviously, it made your jaw sore and everything sore. "So then, I get a chip, and it's like, 'What does this let me do?' Immediately, controlling a computer is like, 'boom.' Portal to the world. You just immediately get your portal to the world back." Rockstar spent 13 years painstakingly crafting the world of GTA 6 to ensure every blade of grass and every line of dialogue was given an unprecedented amount of detail. Although it's maybe truer to life than some may have hoped, there's no denying that the amount of freedom the studio gives players to do everything from robbing banks to diving for sunken treasure has attracted tens of millions of players . Despite guiding Jason and Lucia through GTA 6 by different means, the Neuralink participant shown today is one of those millions. In a follow-up post, the tech company, which was co-founded by controversial figure and billionaire Elon Musk, reiterated that the participant and others like him are part of an extremely limited clinical trial. "Neuralink devices are investigational and have not been approved by the FDA or other regulatory authorities," it said. "This content features voluntary clinical trial participants sharing their personal experiences, which may not reflect all participants or future outcomes." The first human patient to enter the Neuralink program used it to stay up all night playing Civilization 6 in 2024. A few months later, he was playing Slay the Spire .
